name: Veeam Data Platform
description: Veeam Data Platform is a unified backup, recovery, and cyber-resilience platform that protects virtual, physical, cloud, and SaaS workloads and lets IT teams recover data to any platform with no vendor lock-in.
best_for: IT and data-protection teams wanting one licensed platform to back up, recover, and secure workloads across on-premises hypervisors, physical servers, and multiple public clouds.
features: Backup and recovery across VMware, Hyper-V, physical servers, Kubernetes, and unstructured data
Multicloud protection for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, plus SaaS workloads including Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Salesforce
AI-powered threat detection that scans backups and restore points for ransomware and malware before recovery
Portable, self-describing backup format for cloud-based disaster recovery without a dedicated DR site
Workload mobility across hypervisors, clouds, and storage with no vendor lock-in
Governance and compliance automation: immutability, retention policies, DR testing, and audit-ready reporting
Data sovereignty controls to keep backup data within jurisdictional boundaries
pros: Published, self-serve per-pack annual pricing across four editions (Essentials, Foundation, Advanced, Premium)
Organization-level SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 (plus 27017, 27018, 22301, and 27701), and HIPAA/HITECH Type 2 attestation, per Veeam's own trust center
Recognized as a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Backup and Data Protection Platforms for the 10th consecutive time, per Veeam's own citation of the report
cons: Licensing is sold in per-instance packs (5 instances for Essentials, 10 for the other editions) rather than a simple per-seat or flat per-device price, which takes some translation to a specific environment's workload count
Only annual, per-pack pricing is published -- no monthly billing option is shown

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.notes: Veeam's own comparison describes Essentials as offering the same features as Advanced, for up to 50 workloads -- positioned for small business.

tiers.name: Foundation
tiers.notes: Marketed as Veeam's "Most Popular" edition on its product page. Backup and recovery for every workload.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.notes: Adds proactive monitoring, analytics, and threat insights over Foundation.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.notes: Adds orchestrated recovery and full cyber-resilience and compliance orchestration over Advanced.

alternatives.name: NinjaOne
alternatives.description: NinjaOne is a unified IT operations platform combining RMM, patch management, backup, remote access, and service-desk ticketing for IT teams and MSPs.
alternatives.best_for: IT teams and MSPs wanting lightweight endpoint, server, and SaaS backup bundled into a broader RMM console rather than a dedicated enterprise data-resilience platform.
strengths: Backup bundled with RMM and patching

alternatives.name: ConnectWise RMM
alternatives.description: ConnectWise RMM is a cloud-based remote monitoring and management platform for MSPs, part of the ConnectWise Platform, with a Backup Dashboard and Microsoft 365 SaaS backup available on its higher packages.
alternatives.best_for: MSPs wanting basic endpoint and Microsoft 365 backup bundled into their RMM package rather than a dedicated enterprise backup and disaster-recovery platform.
strengths: Microsoft 365 SaaS backup on the Premium package
Backup Dashboard visibility across managed endpoints
Bundled with broader RMM, patching, and remote access

faq.question: How is Veeam Data Platform licensed and priced?
faq.answer: Veeam sells Veeam Data Platform in per-instance license packs billed annually, across four editions. As of the last verified date, Essentials starts at $475/year for a 5-instance pack, and Foundation, Advanced, and Premium start at $1,550, $1,890, and $2,275/year respectively for 10-instance packs.

faq.question: Is Veeam itself SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certified?
faq.answer: Yes. Per Veeam's own trust center, Veeam holds organization-level SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 (along with 27017, 27018, 22301, and 27701) certifications, plus a HIPAA/HITECH Type 2 attestation, rather than only helping customers achieve their own compliance.
